suggestions.reason: The clause clearly defines what the Consultant is engaged to perform and establishes a process for additional services, but it fails to state expressly what falls outside the scope of the Contract Services. This omission creates a bilateral risk: the Consultant may face informal pressure to perform work beyond Exhibit A without additional compensation, while the City may have no clear textual basis to reject deliverables or claims tied to undefined out-of-scope activities. Without an explicit out-of-scope boundary, disputes over whether a particular task was included in the base engagement are likely, and neither party has a neutral reference point. A single sentence anchoring out-of-scope services to the existing written supplemental agreement mechanism resolves this gap without shifting advantage to either party.
suggestions.original_text: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services ("Contract Services") described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. Any services not expressly described in Exhibit A are outside the scope of the Contract Services and shall not be performed by Consultant without a written supplemental agreement or amendment signed by the Parties. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City's request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

suggestions.reason: This provision is a bare referential clause that delegates all material commercial terms — fee basis, invoicing, payment timing, late payment consequences, expense treatment, and dispute rights — exclusively to Exhibit A, without retaining any operative fallback terms in the body of the Agreement. If Exhibit A is silent, incomplete, or disputed, neither party has an enforceable payment framework to rely upon, exposing the City to uncontrolled fee escalation and the Consultant to collection risk. Market-standard professional services agreements incorporate at minimum a payment due date, a late payment remedy, and an expense approval requirement directly in the operative section, regardless of what Exhibit A provides.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A (which shall specify the basis of fee calculation and applicable rates), the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services performed as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement, within thirty (30) days following receipt of each invoice. The City may dispute any invoice by written notice (email sufficing) within ten (10) days of receipt, and undisputed amounts shall be paid by the due date; late undisputed payments shall accrue interest at [__]% per month from the due date. Reimbursable expenses, if any, shall be limited to those pre-approved in writing by the City and set forth in Exhibit A.

suggestions.reason: The termination clause presents three bilateral fairness deficiencies. First, "cause" is used without definition, leaving both parties exposed to disputes over whether a triggering event qualifies. Second, and most critically, the clause contains no cure period for termination for cause: either party may issue a notice and terminate at the end of sixty days even where the other party could readily remedy the underlying breach, which is below market standard for professional services agreements. Third, the Consultant's termination right is drafted as convenience-only, while the City retains both convenience and cause grounds, creating an asymmetry that is not commercially justified. Note: The express survival of indemnity and insurance provisions should be confirmed against the Agreement's general survival clause to ensure no inconsistency.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days’ written notice for convenience or cause upon written notice to Consultant. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days’ written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice to Consultant, or for cause (including material breach or insolvency) upon written notice specifying the breach in reasonable detail if Consultant fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days following receipt of such notice. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate this Agreement at any time for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice to the City, or for cause (including material breach or insolvency of the City) upon written notice specifying the breach in reasonable detail if the City fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days following receipt of such notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes compliance obligations solely on the Consultant and omits several market-standard elements that expose both parties to material legal and commercial risk: it contains no anti-bribery or anti-corruption obligation, no requirement to notify the other party of a material legal breach affecting performance, no allocation of costs when a change in law increases the burden of compliance, and no reference to forced labor or human trafficking standards applicable to the Consultant's supply chain. The unilateral compliance and indemnification structure also creates an imbalance — the City bears no reciprocal compliance duty or indemnification exposure for its own legal violations. Left unaddressed, these gaps could result in undetected regulatory breaches, unallocated change-in-law costs, and enforcement risk for either party. Note: Ensure this Section is cross-referenced in any applicable Survival clause to preserve indemnification obligations following expiration or termination of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Each party shall comply with applicable local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws (including anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws and applicable forced labor and human trafficking laws) pertaining to this Agreement, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement; each party shall bear its own costs of complying with any change in applicable law; and each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any material violation of applicable law that affects its performance under this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on Consultant's violation of the same, and the City shall indemnify and hold harmless Consultant against any claim or liability arising from or based on the City's violation of the same.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules
suggestions.reason: The clause addresses anti-discrimination obligations but leaves three material compliance gaps that expose both parties: it contains no anti-bribery or anti-corruption obligation, no supply chain labor standard addressing forced labor or human trafficking, and no requirement for either party to notify the other upon becoming aware of a material breach of applicable law affecting the Agreement. These omissions are commercially significant for a Professional Services Agreement, as regulators and counterparties increasingly treat anti-corruption and supply chain integrity as threshold compliance requirements, and the absence of a mutual breach-notification obligation means a non-breaching party may remain unaware of a legal violation until material harm has occurred.
suggestions.original_text: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age. Each party shall also comply with all applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and supply chain labor laws (including applicable laws prohibiting forced labor and human trafficking) in connection with this Agreement, and shall notify the other party in writing within ten (10) Business Days of becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law affecting performance of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The insurance obligation is bounded only to "the duration of this Agreement," leaving a gap for claims-made or late-discovered professional liability claims that arise after expiration or termination — a risk exposure for both parties under a professional services relationship. Additionally, the clause is silent on whether the specified insurance requirements constitute a ceiling on either party's liability, which creates ambiguity: a court or claimant could argue that the contractual insurance floor implicitly caps recovery, undermining any broader indemnification or liability provisions elsewhere in the Agreement. Both omissions are market-standard items in professional services agreements and should be addressed to protect the commercial expectations of both the City and the Consultant.
suggestions.original_text: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.
suggestions.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement and for a period of three (3) years following expiration or termination of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The insurance requirements set forth herein establish minimum coverage obligations only and shall not be construed to limit or otherwise affect either party's liability under this Agreement. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement's execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

suggestions.reason: The opening phrase "Without in any way limiting" creates material uncertainty by implying this indemnity sits entirely outside any limitation of liability provisions elsewhere in the Agreement, leaving both parties without a clear ceiling on financial exposure. The notice obligation runs only one way—requiring Consultant to notify the City—while omitting Consultant's right to control the defense and the City's corresponding duty to cooperate, both of which are market-standard procedural protections for a functioning indemnity regime. Additionally, the clause imposes no mitigation obligation on the City, exposing Consultant to losses the City could reasonably have limited. Note: Ensure this Section is expressly enumerated in the Agreement's survival clause to remain operative following expiration or termination.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Subject to any limitation of liability provisions set forth in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant's services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant's services. Consultant shall give the City prompt written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision, and Consultant shall have the right to control the defense and settlement of any such claim; the City shall cooperate reasonably in such defense and shall take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate any resulting loss or damages.

suggestions.reason: This clause contains five material deficiencies that create legal uncertainty for both parties. First, it names no governing law and identifies no binding forum, leaving the phrase "free to take such steps as it deems necessary" to grant the initiating party an entirely unilateral and unrestricted choice of venue or remedy — a commercially asymmetric result that exposes either party to surprise litigation in an inconvenient or unexpected forum. Second, the pre-dispute negotiation step sets no timeframe, which means either party could indefinitely delay or immediately bypass formal proceedings with no contractual consequence. Third, there is no carve-out preserving each party's right to seek emergency injunctive or equitable relief, which is a material omission in a professional services context where breach of confidentiality or IP obligations may require immediate court action. Finally, the obligation to continue performance during a dispute is imposed solely on the Consultant and not on the City, creating an asymmetric operational burden that undermines bilateral fairness.
suggestions.original_text: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement should first be addressed by negotiations between the parties. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, the party initiating the claim that is the basis of the dispute shall be free to take such steps as it deems necessary to protect its interest; provided, however, that notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 11. Disputes. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of [State]. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement shall first be addressed by good-faith negotiations for thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute. If negotiations fail to resolve the dispute within such period, either party may pursue resolution exclusively in the state or federal courts of [County/State], each party hereby consenting to such jurisdiction; provided, however, that either party may seek emergency injunctive or equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction without first exhausting the negotiation period. Notwithstanding any such dispute, both the City and Consultant shall continue to perform their respective obligations under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.

suggestions.reason: The existing Representations clause is limited to a single anti-collusion statement, leaving the Agreement entirely without any warranty as to the standard of performance, compliance with applicable laws, non-infringement of third-party rights, the period during which warranties apply, or any remedy for a breach — all of which are market-standard requirements in a Professional Services Agreement. Without a performance standard, neither party has an objective benchmark against which the quality of the Services can be measured or disputed, creating significant enforceability risk on both sides. The absence of a non-infringement warranty and a law-compliance warranty further exposes both parties to downstream liability with no contractual basis for recourse or allocation of responsibility. Note: To the extent the warranty obligations added below survive termination or expiration of this Agreement, they should be expressly enumerated in the Agreement's Survival clause.
suggestions.original_text: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.
suggestions.suggested_fix: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion. Provider further warrants that the Services will be performed with reasonable skill and care, that the Services and all deliverables will not infringe any third party's intellectual property rights, and that each party shall comply with all applicable laws in connection with this Agreement. These warranties shall apply for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery of the relevant Services or deliverables. In the event of a breach of any warranty set forth in this Section, Provider shall, within thirty (30) days of receipt of written notice specifying the breach, re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if re-performance is not practicable, refund the fees paid for such non-conforming Services or deliverables.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation is made exclusively by the Consultant, leaving no equivalent warranty from the Client that it, too, has the legal capacity and corporate authorization to enter into and perform this Agreement. This asymmetry creates an enforcement gap: if the Client later lacks proper authorization, the Consultant has no contractual basis to challenge the Agreement's validity or hold the Client to its obligations. As a matter of market-standard practice in professional services agreements, authority representations are made mutually by both parties.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party represents and warrants that it has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement, and that the individuals who have signed this Agreement on its behalf have the legal power, right, and authority to make this Agreement and to bind such party.

suggestions.reason: This clause imposes broad, open-ended warranties solely on the Consultant using undefined and inherently subjective benchmarks — "recognized professional standards prevalent in their field," "state of the art procedures and techniques," and "ready comprehension of the required subject matter" — none of which are defined in the Agreement, making the standard of performance practically unenforceable and highly susceptible to dispute. The absence of a materiality qualifier means even a minor or technical deviation could constitute a breach, creating disproportionate and uncapped liability exposure for the Consultant. At the same time, the Client bears no reciprocal obligation to provide the information, materials, or access necessary to enable the Consultant's performance, rendering the clause commercially one-sided. These combined deficiencies create material enforceability risk for both parties and warrant objective anchoring of the performance standard, a materiality threshold, and a minimal Client cooperation obligation.
suggestions.original_text: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement, shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and service performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall conform, in all material respects, to generally accepted professional standards in the Consultant's field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of commercially reasonable procedures and techniques applicable to the Services. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the expertise to provide such services. In support thereof, Client shall provide Consultant with reasonably necessary information, materials, and access as Consultant may reasonably request in writing.

suggestions.reason: The current clause imposes an assignment restriction solely on Consultant while leaving the City entirely free to assign or transfer its rights and obligations without restriction, creating a material bilateral imbalance that is uncommercial in a standard professional services arrangement. The absence of any standard governing consent — such as a "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" qualifier or a response timeframe — exposes Consultant to indefinite withholding of consent with no recourse. The clause also fails to address permitted assignments to affiliates or in connection with a merger or acquisition, provides no requirement to notify the non-assigning party of a permitted transfer, and does not preserve the assigning party's continuing liability for its obligations post-assignment, leaving both parties commercially exposed in a change-of-control scenario.
suggestions.original_text: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant without the prior written consent of the City. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant, whether consented to or not.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by either party without the prior written consent of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that either party may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or to a successor entity in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets upon prior written notice to the other party, and in each case the assigning party shall remain liable for its obligations hereunder unless expressly released in writing by the other party. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the permitted successors and assigns of each party.

suggestions.reason: The notice block sets out a fixed address for Columbia Capital Management, LLC but contains no mechanism permitting either party to update its notice details over time. Without such a provision, notices sent to a stale address could be deemed ineffective, creating disputed delivery and triggering disputes over whether contractual deadlines were properly triggered or met. Market-standard Notices clauses invariably include a brief change-of-address mechanism to avoid this uncertainty for both parties.
suggestions.original_text: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204
suggestions.suggested_fix: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204. Either party may change its notice address or designated recipient by providing written notice to the other party, such change to be effective ten (10) Business Days following receipt of such notice.

suggestions.reason: The clause omits three market-standard elements that are essential to a legally defensible independent contractor provision: it does not state that Consultant controls the manner and means of performance (a critical factor in employment-classification analyses under common law and IRS tests); it does not establish bilateral responsibility for each party's own personnel costs, taxes, and benefits (the current drafting imposes tax obligations solely on Consultant while leaving the City's reciprocal obligations unstated); and it does not confirm that neither party has authority to bind the other, leaving both parties exposed to apparent-agency liability. Left uncorrected, these gaps could support a worker-misclassification claim, create ambiguity as to employment status, or expose either party to unauthorized commitments made by the other's personnel.
suggestions.original_text: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor who shall control the manner and means of performing the services hereunder. Each party shall be responsible for and pay all taxes, withholdings, and employment-related costs required by law with respect to its own personnel, and Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection with Consultant's failure to satisfy such obligations. Neither party shall have authority to bind the other in any manner. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law
suggestions.reason: Although this section addresses the City's statutory appropriations constraint under Kansas law, it is silent on three market-standard compliance obligations that carry meaningful legal and operational exposure for both parties: anti-bribery and anti-corruption conduct, supply-chain labor standards (including prohibitions on forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking), and a reciprocal duty to notify the other party of any law breach that materially affects performance under the Agreement. The absence of these provisions leaves both the City and the service provider without contractual recourse or early-warning mechanisms in the event of a compliance failure by either side. Adding brief, bilateral obligations addressing these gaps aligns the section with standard public-sector professional services contracting practice without disturbing the appropriations mechanism already in place.
suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 17. Compliance with Applicable Laws. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City's current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein. Each party shall comply with all applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws and shall maintain reasonable supply-chain standards against forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any breach of applicable law that materially affects performance under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The current governing law provision does no more than designate Kansas law, leaving the parties with no agreed forum, no pre-dispute escalation obligation, no mutual submission to jurisdiction, no carve-out for emergency injunctive relief, and no obligation to continue performing while a dispute is pending. Without a designated forum, either party may litigate in any court it finds convenient, exposing both sides to parallel or competing proceedings. The absence of a pre-dispute negotiation step and a performance-continuation obligation increases litigation costs and could allow a dissatisfied party to halt performance the moment a dispute arises, magnifying commercial disruption for both sides.
suggestions.original_text: Section 19. Governing Law. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 19. Governing Law; Dispute Resolution. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas. Prior to commencing formal proceedings, the parties shall negotiate in good faith for thirty (30) days following written notice of a dispute. Thereafter, any unresolved dispute shall be submitted exclusively to the state or federal courts located in Kansas, to whose personal and subject-matter jurisdiction both parties irrevocably submit. Each party retains the right to seek emergency injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction without prejudice to the foregoing. Both parties shall continue to perform their respective obligations under this Agreement pending final resolution of any dispute.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements" introduces meaningful ambiguity: it implies the provision self-corrects without any judicial or party action, whereas reformation is ordinarily a remedy effected by a court of competent jurisdiction, not a self-executing contractual mechanism. Two reasonable lawyers could read this differently — one treating it as an operative self-amendment, another as merely aspirational — leaving both parties uncertain about the actual legal status of the reformed provision and potentially undermining the enforceability of any substituted term. Replacing "automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform" with "be deemed reformed and amended to the minimum extent necessary to conform" anchors the reform to a recognized legal standard (minimum necessary modification) and uses the market-standard "deemed" construct, eliminating the ambiguity without altering the clause's core severability purpose.
suggestions.original_text: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall be deemed reformed and amended to the minimum extent necessary to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.

suggestions.reason: The clause addresses the effect of a party's failure to enforce a right (passive non-enforcement), but omits the equally important principle that an express or implied waiver of one specific breach or right does not operate as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach, right, or provision. Without this language, a party that grants a one-time accommodation — such as accepting a late deliverable or overlooking a minor compliance failure — risks an argument by the counterparty that the same conduct is now permanently tolerated. This gap creates enforceability uncertainty for both parties and is a standard element of market-form waiver clauses in professional services agreements.
suggestions.original_text: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any breach of any term or provision hereof shall be construed as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach, or of any other right or remedy. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.

suggestions.reason: The current Amendments clause, while requiring a written and signed instrument, leaves three material gaps that create enforceability risk for both parties equally: it does not specify that authorized representatives must sign on behalf of each party, leaving signature authority ambiguous; it does not expressly extend the amendment requirement to Schedules and Order Forms, which could permit a court to treat modifications to those attachments as outside the clause's scope; and it contains no express anti-oral-modification or anti-course-of-conduct language, exposing both parties to claims that informal communications or conduct modified the Agreement's terms. Together, these omissions reduce the practical enforceability of the written-amendment requirement and create unnecessary litigation risk.
suggestions.original_text: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement, including all Schedules and Order Forms, may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by an authorized representative of each party, and no oral agreement or course of conduct shall constitute or evidence an amendment hereto.

suggestions.reason: The survivorship clause expressly names only Consultant's post-termination obligations — Insurance and Indemnification — while omitting any reference to Client's corresponding obligations, most critically the obligation to pay fees accrued prior to termination. This asymmetry creates an enforcement gap that disadvantages the Consultant (whose post-termination obligations are expressly preserved and therefore clearly enforceable) while leaving Client-side duties to implied survival at best. Additionally, the catch-all phrase "any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination" is insufficiently objective: two courts could reach different conclusions on which provisions qualify, exposing both parties to dispute over the post-termination enforceability of key obligations such as confidentiality, intellectual property ownership, and limitation of liability. Replacing the vague catch-all with the market-standard formulation "by their express terms or necessary implication" provides a more judicially recognized and objectively determinable standard, reducing litigation risk for both parties.
suggestions.original_text: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant’s obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant's obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), Client's obligation to pay any fees accrued prior to the effective date of termination, and any other provisions that by their express terms or by necessary implication are intended to survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The compliance obligation in this clause runs solely against Consultant — requiring it to act in accordance with the Agreement and "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" — while imposing no corresponding duty on the City to perform its own obligations under the Agreement, creating an unjustified enforcement asymmetry between the parties. Without a reciprocal compliance obligation on the City, Consultant lacks an express contractual basis to hold the City to the Agreement's terms. Additionally, the phrase "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" is objectively ambiguous: it identifies no defined legal standard and could yield conflicting interpretations in a dispute over Consultant's conduct or liability. Replacing this phrase with an objective standard and mirroring the compliance duty across both parties restores bilateral balance and enforceability clarity.
suggestions.original_text: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the “Accounts”). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the "Accounts"). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, each Party agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing its respective obligations hereunder.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes a full fiduciary standard on Consultant without cross-referencing any limitation of liability provision, meaning the open-ended "care, skill, prudence, and diligence" obligation could expose Consultant to uncapped financial liability for any alleged shortfall in asset management performance, while Client bears no corresponding obligation. Additionally, the benchmark of "an enterprise of like character and with like aims" is undefined within the Agreement, leaving a court to rely on extrinsic evidence to determine the applicable standard of care, which creates interpretive uncertainty for both parties. Anchoring the prudent-person benchmark to the investment objectives stated in the Agreement and subordinating this clause to the Agreement's limitation of liability provision would address both deficiencies in a commercially balanced manner. Note: Ensure this clause is expressly addressed in the Agreement's limitation of liability and survival provisions to confirm the intended scope of Consultant's ongoing exposure.
suggestions.original_text: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. Subject to the limitations set forth in Section [X] (Limitation of Liability), as a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims, as determined by reference to the investment objectives and guidelines expressly set forth in this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The obligation to "timely" provide balances, account statements, and interest earned is unenforceable in practice because "timely" imposes no objectively measurable standard — neither party has a clear benchmark against which performance or breach can be assessed. Without a defined frequency or deadline, the City cannot demonstrate compliance and the Consultant cannot pursue a remedy for delayed information, creating a commercially unworkable obligation. Additionally, the clause does not identify the triggering condition — whether delivery is periodic, event-driven, or on-demand — leaving both parties without a clear framework for when the obligation arises.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts within five (5) Business Days following the close of each calendar month.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "respond to Consultant's requests" is operationally ambiguous — a court could reasonably read it as requiring mere acknowledgment of a request rather than actual execution of the transfer, exposing both parties to a dispute over whether the City's duty was performed. Additionally, "investment plan" is not capitalized or defined anywhere in the clause, leaving the scope of permissible transfer instructions open to competing interpretations. Finally, the clause imposes a broadly worded obligation on the City with no carve-out protecting it from instructions that may conflict with applicable law or the City's own treasury policies, creating an unreasonable unilateral burden without a corresponding protective limit.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant’s requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City’s various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request and with reasonable notice, comply with Consultant's written requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City's various accounts as necessary to effect the Investment Plan, subject to applicable law and the City's treasury policies.

suggestions.reason: This clause places the entire operational and financial burden of Custodian instruction squarely on the City — including all settlement expenses — while imposing no defined obligation on Consultant regarding the timeliness, accuracy, or delivery of the trade confirmations that functionally trigger the City's duty to act. The phrase "copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant" is undefined, leaving open whether informal communications suffice, and the clause contains no temporal anchor requiring either Consultant to deliver confirmations or the City to instruct the Custodian within a specified period, creating material settlement-failure exposure for both parties. As a matter of bilateral commercial fairness, Consultant's confirmation-delivery obligation and the City's corresponding instruction obligation should each be tied to objective timeframes to make the operational condition precedent enforceable and unambiguous.
suggestions.original_text: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1), the City shall, within two (2) Business Days following receipt of written trade confirmations from Consultant, instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with such written trade confirmations; provided that Consultant shall deliver such written trade confirmations to the Custodian and the City within one (1) Business Day following execution of each transaction.

suggestions.reason: The clause addresses Consultant's conflict-avoidance policy in some detail but contains a material gap: neither party is required to disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest to the other. Without an affirmative disclosure obligation, the City has no contractual mechanism to learn of conflicts that may affect its accounts, and Consultant has no documented duty to surface them, creating both legal exposure and a breakdown of informed consent that undermines the clause's protective intent. From a bilateral commercial perspective, an undisclosed conflict that later affects investment performance or bond-purchasing decisions could expose both parties to regulatory scrutiny and civil liability. This disclosure gap should be addressed by inserting a concise, affirmative obligation on Consultant to disclose actual or potential conflicts in writing promptly upon becoming aware of them.
suggestions.original_text: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an “Issuer Client”), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. Consultant shall promptly disclose to the City in writing any actual or potential conflict of interest of which Consultant becomes aware that could reasonably affect the City's Accounts. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.

suggestions.reason: The City's unilateral right to amend Schedule X "at any time" with only unspecified "notice" to Consultant creates a material imbalance: Consultant is bound by amended authority designations with no guaranteed advance warning, leaving it unable to verify instructions or adjust operations before changes take effect, which undermines both parties' ability to manage the engagement reliably. The absence of a defined notice period renders the amendment mechanism commercially ambiguous — a court could not determine whether notice given one hour before an amendment is effective satisfies the clause. Additionally, the phrase "does not identify the City" in the aggregate data permission lacks objective precision; without a "directly or indirectly" qualifier, two reasonable readers would disagree on whether contextual or inferential identification is prohibited, creating a latent enforcement dispute. Note also that "Schedule X" appears to be an unfilled placeholder and must be replaced with the correct designated schedule reference before execution.
suggestions.original_text: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing by the City upon at least ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not directly or indirectly identify the City.

suggestions.reason: The clause establishes the fee calculation methodology and billing frequency but omits several market-standard commercial terms that create material risk for both parties: there is no stated payment due date, no mechanism for either party to dispute an invoice or treat disputed amounts, no consequence for late payment, and no provision addressing whether and how the fee rate may be adjusted over the life of the Agreement. Additionally, while the clause states that the specified amount is the "sole compensation" for investment advisory services, it does not expressly address whether out-of-pocket expenses are excluded from or included within that statement, leaving expense reimbursement ambiguous. These omissions expose Consultant to collection uncertainty and Client to unchecked fee changes or unilateral expense pass-throughs, and are not consistent with market-standard professional services fee provisions.
suggestions.original_text: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Consultant may adjust the foregoing fee rate upon no less than sixty (60) days' prior written notice to Client. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement, excluding pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses. Client may dispute any invoice in writing (email sufficing) within fifteen (15) days of receipt; undisputed amounts shall remain due and payable, and late payment of undisputed amounts shall accrue interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies" is grammatically incomplete and ambiguous—a court could reasonably read it as the City directing how the Custodian votes or simply directing that the Custodian vote, leaving the scope of the City's obligation unclear. Additionally, the clause creates an asymmetry by absolving the Consultant of all proxy-voting responsibility without expressly making the City solely responsible for all proxy-voting decisions, so the corresponding burden on the City is implied rather than stated, creating a gap in accountability. These two deficiencies together risk a dispute over who bears responsibility if a proxy is voted incorrectly or not voted at all.
suggestions.original_text: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies and Consultant shall have no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian with respect to the voting of all proxies, and the City shall be solely responsible therefor; Consultant shall have no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies.

suggestions.reason: The clause addresses only Consultant's registration under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 and omits three commercially material elements: a general warranty of compliance with all applicable laws, a representation that the Services will not infringe third-party intellectual property rights, and any remedy available to the City upon a breach of the foregoing representations. Without a non-infringement warranty, the City bears the unallocated risk of third-party intellectual property claims arising from Consultant's work product. The absence of a stated breach remedy creates enforcement uncertainty for both parties, as neither the correction standard nor the refund entitlement is contractually defined. Note: Ensure any breach-of-warranty remedy and survival obligations are expressly enumerated in the Agreement's Survival clause.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant (i) is registered as an “investment adviser” under the Investment  Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the “Consultants Act”); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; and (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant (i) is registered as an "investment adviser" under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the "Consultants Act"); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act; (iv) is and shall remain in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations in connection with its performance under this Agreement; and (v) the Services and all deliverables provided hereunder shall not infringe the intellectual property rights of any third party. In the event of a breach of any of the foregoing representations, Consultant shall, at the City's election, re-perform the affected Services or refund fees paid therefor.

suggestions.reason: The clause declares a fiduciary status but fails to articulate any objective performance standard — such as the skill and care of a qualified professional — against which Consultant's conduct can be measured, leaving both parties without a workable benchmark for evaluating compliance or establishing breach. Equally, the provision omits any temporal scope, creating genuine ambiguity as to whether the fiduciary obligation is confined to the Term or extends beyond termination, which affects both Consultant's post-termination exposure and the counterparty's ability to bring claims. Without these two foundational elements, the clause is commercially incomplete and difficult to enforce as drafted.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement;
suggestions.suggested_fix: During the Term, Consultant is a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement and shall exercise the skill and care of a qualified professional in performing its obligations hereunder;

suggestions.reason: The authority representation runs only one way: the Consultant warrants its capacity to enter and perform this Agreement, but the Company makes no equivalent representation. In a bilateral professional services relationship, the absence of a reciprocal authority representation for the Company creates an asymmetric enforceability gap — if the Company lacked proper authorization, the Consultant would have no contractual basis to challenge the validity of the Agreement or seek recourse. Market-standard drafting requires both parties to mutually warrant their authorization and power to bind their respective organizations.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party represents and warrants that it is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement, and that the execution and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or organizational action.
